podcasts.title: Superintelligence Needs the Physical World with CEO and Co-Founder of Arda Bob McGrew
podcasts.transcript:
Bob McGrew: If you look around
outside, how different is anything from 10 years ago before AI happened? Not very different at all. The first time you were in your Waymo,
you thought to yourself, "This is amazing." Probably the third time
you're in your Waymo, you're like, "Man, this traffic sucks." We need to break
out of this pure focus on the digital world and go to the physical world. I don't think you are actually gonna
be able to get to super intelligence without changes in the physical world. Sarah Guo: Hi listeners. Welcome back to No Priors. Today, Elad and I are here with Bob
McGrew, the CEO and co-founder of Arda. Bob was previously an early key
exec at Palantir and the chief research officer at OpenAI. We talk about making American
manufacturing competitive with intelligence, why physical intelligence is
necessary for super intelligence, and why the future is going to be machines that
can make machines and explore the stars. Welcome Bob. Elad Gil: Bob, thanks so much for
joining us today on No Priors. Bob McGrew: Great to be here. Elad Gil: Yeah. So you've had a ridiculous career. You were the chief research officer at
OpenAI, so you drove all the sort of research directions for the company,
or at least set a lot of the agenda. You were at Palantir quite early
and one of the main people there driving product and engineering. So you've had this amazing career
spanning some of the most seminal moments of the digital world, and yet
now you're working in the physical world. And it's right in the arrow when
people are talking about RSI, which is recursive self-improvement, about how
we will no longer have researchers, they'll be displaced by code and AI
and, you know, AI building itself. Why do anything in the physical
world right now as this digital revolution is happening? Bob McGrew: Well, you know, fundamentally,
I don't think you are actually gonna be able to get to super intelligence
without changes in the physical world. So, you know, the-- we've seen
a huge amount of improvement from ChatGPT, from agents. You know, all of this is happening in our
digital lives, and very little of that has actually affected the atoms of our lives. Like, if you look around outside-
How different is anything from 10 years ago before AI happened? Sarah Guo: Mm-hmm. Bob McGrew: You know, not
very different at all. You know, even when you're doing something
that is genuinely very different, maybe you're in a self-driving car, right? You're, you know, in a self-driving
car, in your Waymo, going around San Francisco, and the first time you
were in your Waymo, you thought to yourself, "This is amazing." Mm-hmm. There's, there's no one driving it. Yeah. The, like, car is driving itself. And, like, probably the third time you're
in your Waymo, you're like, "Traffic." Elad Gil: Mm-hmm. "
Bob McGrew: Man, this traffic sucks." Elad Gil: Yeah. Bob McGrew: Right? Because just… You
know, you have something. Even, you know, a Waymo
is, like- I got that. I feel that … halfway
towards the physical world. Yeah. But, like, you didn't change the car. Like, the car doesn't fly. You're still bounded by all of the

world and go to the physical world. Elad Gil: So when you say you can't
have super intelligence without changing the physical world,

work of the researcher, that you're gonna be able to unleash a runaway acceleration,

accumulated in the right places? Was it connected together
with the right networks? And so, um, you can, you know,
completely automate researchers. This is a big effect, right? I'm not saying this is not a big deal. You know, maybe this is even, maybe
